prompt: Which pair describes an uptrend structure?

explanations.b: Lower highs and lower lows describe a downtrend.
explanations.c: Equal highs and lower lows do not match either trend. The highs are not rising.
explanations.d: One up candle is not a pattern of swings. An uptrend needs successive higher highs and higher lows.

prompt: Hypothetical. Swing sequence in time order: low 100, high 120, low 110, high 125, low 115. In an uptrend, what is the structure-break level, in rupees?
solution: In an uptrend, the structure-break level is the most recent swing low. The most recent swing low in this sequence is 115. Check: the lows run 100, 110, 115, so 115 is the last one.

prompt: Hypothetical. Swing highs are 250, then 252, then 250. Swing lows are 240, then 238, then 240. How should the structure be classified?

options.text: Uptrend, because the last high is above the first
Downtrend, because the last low is below the first
Range, because the highs and lows do not rise or fall together
Cannot be classified without a volume figure

explanations.a: The highs do not rise in a line. The high of 252 is followed by 250, which is a lower high.
explanations.b: The lows do not fall in a line. The low of 238 is followed by 240, which is a higher low.
explanations.d: Structure uses swing points, not volume. The swing points here are enough to classify the structure.

prompt: Hypothetical. A trader says: 'Price made a new high on one day, so the trend is up.' What is the best reply?

options.text: Agreed. A new high is enough to call a trend.
One new high is one point. A trend needs successive swing points, so check the higher lows as well.
Agreed, but only if the day closed higher.
The trend is down, because a new high always means a reversal.

explanations.a: A single new high is not enough. A trend needs successive swing points.
explanations.c: A close higher on one day still does not make a trend. The swing sequence must show the pattern.
explanations.d: A new high does not always mean a reversal. The swing sequence decides the label, not one high.

prompt: Spot the mistake: 'I first used a swing high with lower highs on both sides within N candles. The chart did not show the trend I wanted, so I changed N to one candle on each side.' Which part is wrong?

options.text: I first used a swing high with lower highs on both sides within N candles
The chart did not show the trend I wanted
So I changed N to one candle on each side

explanations.a: This part is correct. A swing definition with N is a valid choice, as long as it is written down first.
explanations.b: This describes a result. It is not the mistake. The mistake is what the trader did after seeing the result.
explanations.d: There is a mistake. Changing the definition after seeing the result is hindsight, and the label is no longer a fair test.

prompt: Hypothetical. Swing sequence in time order: high 260, low 240, high 255, low 238. For a downtrend view, what is the structure-break level, in rupees?
solution: For a downtrend view, the structure-break level is the most recent swing high. That is 255. A close above 255 means the last lower high has failed. Check: the highs run 260, then 255, so 255 is the most recent one.
